brow: Aggregated snapshot · open-source compilation · not official reporting
editionNote: Morning edition. It covers the 24 hours to 05:10 CET on 2 November; new research covers 17:10 CET on 1 November to 05:10 CET on 2 November, items from the previous edition still inside the 24 hours were carried, and stories with new developments are marked as follow-ups.

theaters.heading: Battlefield, long-range strikes, and peace diplomacy in Russia's war on Ukraine

items.title: Zelensky Offers to Halt Refinery Strikes if the US Sells Ukraine Patriots
items.lede: Kyiv's leader tied any pause to faster US interceptor deliveries, saying Ukraine would pay for a month of missiles and hold fire for the same month.

sections.text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told Fox News on Sunday that Ukraine would stop striking Russian oil refineries if the United States quickly supplied Patriot interceptors [1][2]. He said a month of missile deliveries would buy a month without refinery strikes [1][2]. He said Ukraine would pay for the missiles rather than rely only on aid [1]. He also said Russia would have to stop attacking Ukraine's energy system [1][2]. The US State Department approved a $2.1 billion sale of Patriot interceptors to Ukraine on 30 October [1]. Zelensky has warned that deliveries of the 500 interceptors could take years [1][2]. President Trump, facing soaring energy prices at home, has pressed Kyiv to stop refinery strikes [1][2]. No White House or Kremlin response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on what Zelensky said, because RFE/RL and the Guardian quote the Fox News interview directly. The interview's exact broadcast time is not established.

items.title: Oleshky Truce Expires as Russia Turns Down Ukraine's Offer to Extend It
items.lede: Kyiv's military moved 167 more civilians out of Kherson-region frontline villages before the six-day pause ended, and the regional governor warned of renewed shelling.

sections.text: Ukraine and Russia observed a local ceasefire around Oleshky, a Russian-occupied town in Ukraine's Kherson region, from 27 October [3][4]. US First Lady Melania Trump brokered the pause [5][6]. Evacuees from the town crossed into Ukraine's Chernihiv region on Saturday, Zelensky said [7]. The truce expired at 22:59 Kyiv time on Sunday (21:59 CET) with no violations reported by either side [8]. A Ukrainian official told AFP that Russia refused Kyiv's offer to extend it [8][1]. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Moscow viewed the operation positively, Russian news agencies reported [8]. On Sunday, Ukraine's General Staff said troops evacuated 167 more civilians from the Ukrainian-held right bank of the Dnipro in Kherson region [8][2]. The group included 22 children and 21 people with limited mobility [8]. Kherson Governor Oleksandr Prokudin urged residents to stay away from settlements near the river [8]. An unnamed Ukrainian officer told AFP that Russian forces used the pause to bring in troops and ammunition [2].

Confidence is high that the truce ended and that 167 people were evacuated, which agencies report from official statements. The refusal to extend rests on one unnamed Ukrainian official, and the troop buildup rests on one unnamed officer.

items.title: Russia Follows Its 433-Drone Night With 326 More Drones Against Ukraine
items.lede: A Sunday strike near a dormitory for displaced families in Vinnytsia region killed a 13-year-old girl and another person, and hundreds of thousands of homes lost power.

sections.text: Russia launched 433 strike and decoy drones at Ukraine from 18:00 Kyiv time on Saturday (17:00 CET), the Air Force said [9][10]. By Sunday morning, air defenses had shot down or jammed 371 of them [9][10][8]. Zelensky said strikes on four regions left hundreds of thousands of families without power [10][8]. Russia then launched 326 attack drones and six S8000 Banderol jet-powered munitions between 06:30 and 19:00 Kyiv time on Sunday, the Air Force said [11]. It said air defenses shot down or jammed 274 of the drones and all six Banderols [11]. On Sunday afternoon, a Russian drone hit the grounds of a dormitory for displaced people in the Koziatyn area of Vinnytsia region [12][13]. The strike killed two people, including a 13-year-old girl, and injured six, the State Emergency Service said [13]. The injured included three 5-year-olds, one of them in serious condition [13]. Al Jazeera, citing the same service, put the death toll at three [8]. No Russian Defense Ministry statement on the strikes on Ukraine was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is moderate on the drone totals, which are the Air Force's own preliminary figures. Confidence is high on the Vinnytsia casualties, which officials reported on record, though one outlet gives a higher death toll.

items.title: Russia's FSB Detains a Minor Over the Moscow Park Threat the US Flagged
items.lede: Russian security officials credited the American tip, saying the suspect posted armed TikTok photos at Tsaritsyno; a concert there was canceled and no attack occurred.

sections.text: The US Embassy in Russia said on Saturday it was aware of a credible threat of a mass-casualty event that day at the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve in Moscow [14][15]. It said the US government was coordinating a response with Russian authorities and told people to avoid the area [15][16]. Russia's FSB security service told state media it had received information from US partners about a planned terrorist attack and was taking action [15][16]. The park was evacuated during a concert and closed, Russian media reported [15][17]. On Sunday, the FSB said it had checked the US information and detained a Russian minor [17][18]. It said he posted TikTok photos of himself in tactical gear holding what looked like a rifle [17][18]. His posts included photos taken at Tsaritsyno with the caption "I found a place," the FSB said [18]. The FSB said his phone showed a neo-Nazi Telegram subscription and searches about mass shootings [17][18]. It said planned public events at the park were canceled, and it thanked the US side [18]. No attack or casualties were reported by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the embassy warning and the detention, which NBC News, Reuters, and Interfax quote on record. The suspect's posts rest only on the FSB's account.

items.title: Zelensky Says Ukraine Also Hit $70 Million in Russian Air Defenses
items.lede: Zelensky said the strikes also hit a Pantsir-S2 and an S-400 command vehicle, and he thanked the Security Service of Ukraine for the attack on the Rostov-region plant.

sections.text: Ukraine's General Staff said its forces struck the Kamensky Combine in Kamensk-Shakhtinsky, in Russia's Rostov region, on the night of 30–31 October [19][20]. It said strike drones and the Navy's Neptune coastal missiles were used [19]. The General Staff said a warehouse of finished goods caught fire and four production workshops were damaged [19][20][21]. It said the plant makes solid rocket fuel for Uragan, Smerch, and Tornado-S rocket launchers and for other missiles [19]. On Sunday, President Zelensky said the Kamensky Combine is involved in Russian missile production [22][23]. He said Ukrainian forces also hit a Pantsir-S2 air defense system and an S-400 Triumf command vehicle [22][23]. He put the value of the air defense assets hit at about $70 million [22][23]. He thanked the Security Service of Ukraine and other units for the strikes [22][23]. No Russian official comment on the plant was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate. Reuters, DW, Ukrinform, and Ukrainska Pravda carry the Ukrainian claims, but the damage and the dollar value rest on Kyiv's own account with no independent confirmation.

items.title: Russian Governor Reports Heavy Damage at a Kstovo Plant After Drone Raid
items.lede: Nizhny Novgorod's governor did not name the site, but monitoring channels identified Lukoil's NORSI refinery, which supplies fuel to Russia's military.

sections.text: Lukoil's NORSI oil refinery in Kstovo, in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region, was reportedly hit by drones overnight into Sunday, the Kyiv Independent reported [24]. Ukrainian monitoring channels Exilenova+ and Supernova+ posted footage of the alleged attack [24]. Independent Russian outlet ASTRA said the refinery was struck and burning [24]. NORSI, Russia's fourth-largest refinery, processes about 15 million to 17 million metric tons of crude a year [24]. It sits about 800 kilometers (500 miles) from Ukraine's border [24]. The plant supplies fuel to Russia's armed forces and the Moscow region [25]. On Sunday morning, Nizhny Novgorod Governor Gleb Nikitin said a massive drone attack caused significant damage to an industrial facility in the Kstovo district [25][26]. He did not name the facility and said more than 100 drones were destroyed, with no casualties reported [25][26]. Nikitin warned of temporary power, hot water, and heating cuts in some homes during repairs [26]. Russia's Defense Ministry said air defenses shot down 235 drones nationwide overnight [25]. No Ukrainian military statement on the refinery was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that a site in the Kstovo district was damaged, because the regional governor said so on record. Confidence is moderate that it was the Lukoil refinery, which rests on monitoring channels and ASTRA relayed by three outlets.

items.title: Kremlin Wants Only the US, Russia, and Ukraine at the First Abu Dhabi Rounds
items.lede: Zelensky has floated November 6 to 10 for the meeting, while a top Putin aide cited Moscow's direct contacts with Washington to keep Europeans out of early rounds.

sections.text: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Friday that preparing for three-way talks on Ukraine in Abu Dhabi does not commit Russia to limiting the fighting [27]. The Kyiv Independent, citing an unnamed senior Ukrainian official, reported that Kyiv suspects Moscow of offering a phone call to avoid an in-person leaders' meeting [28]. Late Friday, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told a news conference in Atlanta that if Zelensky wants to meet Putin, he can come to Moscow [29]. Late Saturday, Zelensky told US interviewer Tony Perkins that the three-way meeting could take place between November 6 and 10 [30]. He said Abu Dhabi was the tentative venue, but neither the dates nor the place were final [30]. He said Ukraine backs the US proposal for technical-level talks [30]. On Sunday, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said at least the first rounds should include only Russia, Ukraine, and the United States [31]. He was asked about European involvement and cited Moscow's working contacts with the Americans [31].

Confidence is high on Peskov's, Lavrov's, Zelensky's, and Ushakov's statements, which Interfax, the Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform, and Reuters carry on record. The dates are tentative by Zelensky's own account. Kyiv's suspicion of a phone-call ploy rests on one outlet and an anonymous official.

theaters.heading: Sabotage, drones, cyber, disinformation, and espionage targeting European states

items.title: Ukraine's Air Raid App Sends Fake Nuclear and Chemical Alerts After a Hack
items.lede: Kyiv blamed Moscow, and hours later Russia's Emergencies Ministry said hackers used its own warning app to spread false information.

sections.text: Ukraine's Air Alert app sent false warnings late Sunday, the Ukrainian Air Force said [1][2]. The alerts began at about 21:47 CET with red-level air raid warnings shown nationwide [1]. Messages then warned of radiation and chemical threats in Kyiv and of street fighting in the capital [1][2]. The app sent all-clear messages at about 22:53 CET [1]. The Air Force said the app had probably suffered hostile interference and that there was no radiation threat [1][3]. Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications blamed Russia in a post on X [2][4]. Ukraine's digital ministry said other alert systems and air raid sirens kept working [3]. Early Monday, Russia's Emergencies Ministry said its mobile app suffered a massive cyberattack that let attackers send false information [2][4]. The BBC said a Ukrainian group claimed it sent fake nuclear strike warnings to Russian users [1]. It was not clear whether the two incidents were linked [3].

Confidence is high that both apps sent false alerts, based on official Ukrainian and Russian statements reported by the BBC, Al Jazeera, DW, and ABC. The Ukrainian claim against Russia's app rests on one BBC line, and no attribution has been independently confirmed.

items.title: Jersey Flights Arrive Normally on Sunday After Two Evenings of Drone Incursions
items.lede: The British Crown Dependency asked UK agencies for counter-drone help, and police still had no suspect after the Friday and Saturday disruptions.

sections.text: Unauthorized drones flew in restricted airspace near Jersey Airport on Friday evening, disrupting flights from Britain to the British Crown Dependency [5]. The first report came at about 20:20 local time (21:20 CET), and further drone activity was reported until about 22:30 (23:30 CET) [6]. Jersey Police Inspector Rob McCallum said officers believed two or three drones had been in the restricted airspace [5]. On Saturday at 21:05 CET, the airport reported fresh drone disruption to inbound flights [7][8]. Three more flights into Jersey were canceled, on top of three on Friday [8]. On Sunday, Jersey government officials and operational partners met to review the response to both evenings [9]. The government said it was making arrangements to reduce the risk of more disruption if drones return Sunday evening [9]. Jersey sought support from UK authorities and was exploring counter-drone technology, the government said [10]. No disruption to Sunday evening's flights was reported, the BBC said late Sunday [11]. No operator, motive, or state link was named by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on both nights of disruption, the Sunday government review, and the quiet Sunday evening, which the BBC, Channel 103, ITV, and Bailiwick Express reported from official statements. The drone count rests on one police estimate.

items.title: Belarusian Hackers Claim 23 Terabytes Stolen From Russia's Statistics Agency
items.lede: The agency denied any leak of protected data, but its main website stayed offline Sunday afternoon after hacker messages appeared on its portals.

sections.text: Russia's state statistics service, Rosstat, said its information resources faced targeted destructive cyberattacks from 29 October to 1 November [12]. Rosstat said its monitoring systems flagged the activity in time and found no database compromise or leak of protected data [12]. It said specialists and law enforcement were working to find out how the attackers got in and who was behind them [12]. Messages from the Belarusian Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow appeared on Rosstat's main website and regional portals, the agency told RBC [13]. The hackers claimed they took 23 terabytes, including data on Russian war losses and documents marked for official use only [13]. The Moscow Times said the claims could not be independently verified [13]. Rosstat's main website was still down Sunday afternoon [13]. Russia has banned both groups as extremist, and they claimed a July 2025 attack on Aeroflot [13].

Confidence is high that Rosstat reported the attacks, based on its statement via Interfax and The Moscow Times. The 23-terabyte theft and the war-loss data rest only on the hackers' unverified claims.

items.title: Britain Flies Its Protector Drone at Home to Track a Russian Frigate
items.lede: The unarmed RAF aircraft gave Royal Navy ships more than 10 hours of surveillance over the English Channel in October, British media reported Sunday.

sections.text: A British Royal Air Force Protector RG1 drone flew its first operational sorties in UK airspace, the UK Ministry of Defence said [14][15]. The unarmed aircraft gave the Royal Navy more than 10 hours of surveillance over the English Channel [14][15]. It supported the destroyer HMS Dauntless and the patrol ship HMS Tyne as they tracked the Russian frigate Neustrashimy [14]. The warships monitored the frigate and accompanying merchant ships through the Channel between 1 and 14 October [14]. Metro said the drone's surveillance ran from 14 to 16 October [15]. RAF helicopters also tracked a Russian intelligence-gathering ship operating near NATO units and a Russian landing ship in the Channel, Metro reported [15]. The ministry did not say how many sorties the drone flew or which sensors it used [14]. No Russian response was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that Britain flew the Protector against the Russian frigate, which Defence Blog and Metro report from the UK Ministry of Defence. The exact sortie dates differ slightly between the two outlets.

items.title: Russia-Linked Cargo Ship Leaves Gotland After Swedish Police Check Its Crew
items.lede: Swedish police found nothing unusual, and the vessel sailed south on Sunday while its operator's reported spy links went unconfirmed.

sections.text: Swedish police boarded a dry-cargo ship at a port on northern Gotland overnight into Saturday [16][17]. Border police checked the crew's travel documents, a Stockholm police spokesperson said [16]. She said everything looked fine and the check turned up nothing unusual [16]. TV4 said the ship is over 80 meters long and belongs to a company previously investigated over Russian hybrid and spying operations [17]. TV4 sources said the crew are Russian citizens and the national special forces unit took part; police declined to confirm either [17]. TV4 said ships from the same company have been linked to drone alerts in other European countries [17]. The ship cast off on Sunday morning and was moving south along Gotland's coast, Kvartal reported, citing TV4 [18]. A source told Dagens Nyheter the crew were seven Russian citizens on a ship flagged in another country [19]. No ship name, arrest, or seizure was reported by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that Swedish police boarded the ship and checked crew papers, which SVT and TV4 report from a police spokesperson. Dagens Nyheter now supports the Russian crew through its own source. The special forces role, the company's history, and the departure rest on TV4 alone, the last relayed by Kvartal.

items.title: Belgium's Prime Minister to See the King After Budget Talks Collapse
items.lede: Bart De Wever's coalition failed overnight to agree on a 10 billion euro savings plan, with one parliamentary week left to pass a budget.

sections.text: Belgium's inner cabinet failed to reach a federal budget deal in talks that began at 21:00 on Sunday, Deputy Prime Minister David Clarinval said overnight [1][2]. Prime Minister Bart De Wever will go to King Philippe on Monday, Belga reported [1]. The coalition is trying to find 10 billion euros in savings by 2029 [2]. De Wever had dropped a general VAT increase, a red line for the liberal MR party [2]. Flemish Socialists in Vooruit and the centrist Les Engagés then pressed for new taxes on the wealthy [2]. RTBF said next week is the last parliamentary window to pass a full budget [2]. Without one, the government must run on monthly stopgap spending [2]. No palace statement on the visit was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate. Belga is the only source read for the failed talks and the royal visit. RTBF supports the background and the start of the meeting.

items.title: Spain Says Four Americans Were Among 69 Killed in the Urda Train Crash
items.lede: All but three victims are now identified, and families of two missing Australians and one Japanese citizen are traveling to Spain.

sections.text: Spain's victim identification body said late on Sunday that four US citizens were among the 69 people killed in Wednesday's crash near Urda [3]. One victim each came from Canada, Japan, Argentina, Mexico, Tunisia, and the Czech Republic, the Guardian reported [3]. Officials had already confirmed 54 Spaniards, one French citizen, and one Portuguese citizen among the dead [3]. A Renfe train hit a stationary Iryo train about 130 km south of Madrid [3]. A control center let the Renfe train move after a safety system halted traffic [3]. The crash comes before Spain's 29 November general election [3].
Confidence is moderate. The Guardian is the only source read for the new nationalities.

items.title: Britain Offers EU Students Cheaper Fees in Exchange for Industrial Program Access
items.lede: British ministers would spend up to £450 million a year on the offer, which hinges on a deal at the 20 November summit in Brussels.

sections.text: The UK government is ready to let EU students pay home fees at British universities, the Guardian reported on Sunday, citing sources [4]. Officials would pay universities as much as £450 million a year to cover the cost [4]. Britain wants entry to the EU's planned Made in Europe industrial program in return [4]. The two sides aim to close a set of deals at the summit on 20 November [4]. Talks have largely settled emissions trading, farm products, and a youth mobility plan [4]. A UK government spokesperson said Britain is building an ambitious relationship with the EU but did not confirm the offer [4].
Confidence is moderate. The Guardian is the only source read and relies on unnamed sources. No EU comment was found by the cutoff.

items.title: French Lawyers Say Antiterror Orders Kept Activists Home During Protests
items.lede: The Interior Ministry cited terrorism prevention, but defense lawyers say most targets were students and farmers with no criminal record.

sections.text: Lawyers and rights groups in France said on Sunday that the government used house-arrest orders to keep some alleged activists from Saturday's protests [5]. One Belfort protester got an Interior Ministry notice after 22:00 on Friday barring travel outside the village through 1 November [5]. The orders cite the need to prevent acts of terrorism, according to documents seen by AFP [5]. Paris lawyer Aïnoha Pascual, who represents six people, said most had never been convicted or held in custody [5]. Marseille lawyer Mathilde Lanté said the antiterror tool was being misused and that courts would not hold hearings within 48 hours [5]. No Interior Ministry comment on the criticism was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate. franceinfo, citing AFP and documents it saw, is the only source read. The number of orders issued nationwide was not reported.

items.title: France's Final Count Shows 779 Arrests After Saturday's Cost-of-Living Marches
items.lede: Paris prosecutors have identified three suspects in the gendarme firebombing, and French unions want workers out on Thursday.

sections.text: France's third Saturday of cost-of-living protests drew 320,000 people nationwide, including 70,000 in Paris [6][7]. The Interior Ministry said police had arrested 565 people nationwide by 21:00 [7][8]. At the dispersal, police used tear gas and baton charges against groups throwing paving stones and a firebomb [6][8]. By 21:00, Paris police reported 79 arrests and five officers hurt, three of them burned by a firebomb [7]. The Interior Ministry said IGPN and IGGN watchdogs had 83 cases since mid-September student protests began, including a Reims marcher's shin seriously injured by a police grenade, franceinfo reported [9][10]. Prosecutors opened an attempted-homicide investigation on Sunday after Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez called the firebombing attempted murder [6][11]. On Sunday, the Interior Ministry put the final count at 779 arrests and 116 officers hurt [12]. Paris prosecutors said Sunday they had identified three black-clad firebombing suspects [12]. Five unions called a national strike for 5 November [12]. The prefecture's order n° 2026-01485, which barred everyone from the Place de la République and Châtelet-Les Halles sectors from 23:00 to 06:00 Saturday and Sunday nights, expired at 06:00 Monday [13][14]. A planned 0.8% riot insurance surcharge from 2027 still needs Conseil d'État validation [15].
Confidence is high on turnout, arrests, and clashes, per franceinfo, the Guardian, and RTBF. Suspects and the strike call rest on franceinfo alone.

items.title: EU Commission Sides With Poland's Parliament in Constitutional Court Fight
items.lede: Justice Commissioner Michael McGrath backed Tusk's camp on appointing judges but stopped short of endorsing the suspension of the court's sidelined leadership.

sections.text: Riot police deployed on Friday evening at Poland's Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw after Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska suspended its president, Bogdan Święczkowski, and vice president, Bartłomiej Sochański, for one month [16]. The court wrote on X that everyone taking part was committing the crime of a coup d'état, as Law and Justice supporters, joined by leader Jarosław Kaczyński, protested outside [17][18]. Polish President Karol Nawrocki canceled his Senegal trip in mid-flight and went to the court at about 01:00, where video showed scuffles with judges at the entrance [17][16]. Korwin-Piotrowska has called the court's general assembly for 3 November [16]. On Sunday evening, she said she would order the assembly to also draw judges for disciplinary cases against Święczkowski and Sochański [19]. On Saturday night, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk vowed in a TV address to see the court overhaul through, saying some matters allow no compromise [20]. EU Justice Commissioner Michael McGrath told Politico Europe on Sunday that appointing the new judges lies with the Sejm, the lower house [21]. He did not endorse the suspension of the court's president and deputy [21].

Confidence is high on the suspension, the court's statement, and Tusk's address, reported by the BBC, El País, ANSA, and the Guardian. Politico Europe reported McGrath's remarks. RMF24 reported the planned disciplinary draw.

items.title: Swiss Arms Maker Says Fire Destroyed Its LBD 40 Production Site
items.lede: Bern prosecutors suspect arson at the Thun plant, which supplies French riot police, and an unverified video tied the attack to Gen Z protests.

sections.text: Swiss arms maker Brügger & Thomet told franceinfo on Sunday that a fire fully destroyed the part of its Thun building where it made and stored LBD 40 launchers [22]. French police use the 40 mm launchers during riots [22]. Bern cantonal police were alerted shortly after 03:10 on 29 October, and nobody was hurt [22]. Police quickly favored a criminal cause, and regional prosecutors appealed for witnesses [22]. The French ecology group Les Soulèvements de la Terre said it received a one-minute video claiming the attack [22]. The clip mentions Switzerland, France, and Germany with Gen Z, franceinfo reported [22]. The video's authenticity had not been established [22]. The company said it would not be intimidated [22].
Confidence is moderate. franceinfo is the only source read, citing the company, Bern police, and prosecutors. No Bern police or prosecutor statement was opened directly by the cutoff.

items.title: Spanish Judge Jails Alleged Blocus Ideologue After a Quiet Barcelona Saturday
items.lede: The 18-year-old is accused of driving a Telegram group that urged the 24 October looting, while police ID checks topped 2,000 on Saturday.

sections.text: Spain's Catalan police and Barcelona city police flooded downtown Barcelona on Saturday afternoon for the Blocus calls, El País reported [23]. The day passed without incidents, and police identified more than 2,000 people in about 10 cities, 1,440 of them in Barcelona [24]. Police took 12 minors carrying items such as balaclavas to a station for their protection until parents collected them [23]. Catalan police had set their top risk level, level 4, for only the second time for a protest since 2019 [25]. A court in Torrent on Saturday ordered the alleged Spanish founder of Blocus jailed after his Friday arrest in Valencia province [25]. Police also had four Telegram channels shut down [25]. The 24 October Barcelona looting ended with 133 arrests, 89 of them minors [23]. On Sunday, a Spanish judge jailed an 18-year-old arrested in Barcelona as an alleged Blocus ideologue, citing signs of conspiracy to cause public disorder [24]. Catalan police accused him of instigating and driving one of the Telegram groups that urged the looting [24].

Confidence is high on the deployment, the quiet day, and the jailing, reported by El País and consistent with RTVE and La Vanguardia. No official Catalan police statement on the jailing was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Latvia Fires a Homemade Interceptor Drone at an Unidentified Object Near Russia
items.lede: The object crossed into Russia before it could be hit, so the army blew up its own Blaze drone near the border, and residents heard the blast.

sections.text: Latvia's National Armed Forces declared an airspace threat in the eastern Krāslava and Ludza municipalities at 17:57 CET on Sunday [1] [2]. Residents received an orange cell broadcast alert, the higher of two levels, which tells people to take shelter indoors [2] [3]. The army said an unidentified flying object left Latvian airspace at 18:16 CET by crossing the border into Russia [2]. The alert ended at 18:30 CET [2]. The army later said it had launched a Latvian-made Blaze interceptor drone in response, LETA reported [3] [4]. The interceptor did not hit the object because it had entered Russia [3] [4]. The army triggered the drone's self-destruct near the border to keep it out of Russian territory, and an explosion was heard nearby [3] [4]. The army did not say what the object was. No Russian statement was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the alert and its timing: the army notice, LSM, LETA via TVNET, and BNS via LRT agree; the object's type and origin are not established.

items.title: Latvian TV Finds Premier Kulbergs's Immigration Adviser Draws Investors Seeking Residence Permits
items.lede: Four of the adviser's eight foreign backers already hold permits, the opposition Progressives allege a conflict of interest, and Kulbergs rejects the charge.

sections.text: Latvian public broadcaster LTV's De facto program reported Sunday that Didzis Dejus, an adviser to Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs, raised money from foreigners seeking residence permits [5]. Dejus advises Kulbergs on immigration and co-owns AM Craft, a Riga firm that prints civil aviation parts [5]. His company SIAPLG.EU drew 400,000 euros from eight investors from India, South Africa, Syria, and the United States [5]. Dejus said four of them have received Latvian residence permits and the rest are still under review [5]. He looked for new investors at a citizenship expo in New Delhi in August [5]. Progressives faction leader Andris Šuvajevs said the facts show at least an apparent conflict of interest [5]. The parliamentary majority rejected the Progressives' request for an explanation [5]. Kulbergs called the scheme fully legal and said it predates Dejus's job in his office [5]. Dejus denied using his post to help his investors [5].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one LTV investigation published by LSM, quoting Dejus, Kulbergs, and opposition lawmakers; no second outlet was read.

items.title: Nausėda's Top Adviser Calls Lithuania's 5% Defense Budget the Bare Minimum
items.lede: The 2027 draft budget cuts defense to 5% of GDP from 5.38% this year, and the state auditor says plans need 5.44%.

sections.text: Deividas Matulionis, chief adviser to Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda, said Sunday that defense spending of 5% of GDP is the minimum, Elta reported via LRT [6]. He told the ELTA savaitė program that the budget should be somewhat larger to meet all goals [6]. He said Lithuania is not dropping its goal of a fully equipped land division by 2030 [6]. He said some purchases of armored vehicles, tanks, and artillery could slip or shrink [6]. The 2027 draft budget sets defense at more than 4.8 billion euros [6]. State Auditor Irena Segalovičienė has said the plans need 5.44% of GDP [6].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one Elta interview report carried by LRT; the budget draft and the auditor's statement were not read directly.

items.title: Latvia Takes the UN Security Council Presidency for the First Time
items.lede: Riga's envoy says she will keep Russia's war in Ukraine high on the agenda, and Latvia chairs the vote for World Court judges on 3 November.

sections.text: Latvia holds the rotating presidency of the UN Security Council in November for the first time, Latvian public broadcaster LSM reported [7]. Latvia will chair all formal and informal council meetings this month [7]. Ambassador Sanita Pavļuta-Deslandes said Latvia wants to keep Russia's war in Ukraine high on the council's agenda [7]. She said Latvia will work to counter Russian propaganda and stop the war from being treated as normal [7]. The council has held 16 official meetings on Ukraine this year, almost all called by Latvia and European allies at Ukraine's request [7]. Latvia will preside over the election of International Court of Justice judges on 3 November [7].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one LSM report quoting the ambassador; the UN's own program of work was not read.

items.title: Lawmaker Says Lithuania's Premier Should Quit Over Plagiarism in His Dissertation
items.lede: Dainius Gaižauskas said an early election would be acceptable, while Mindaugas Sinkevičius admits citation errors but defends the thesis's scientific value.

sections.text: Lithuanian lawmaker Dainius Gaižauskas of the Farmers and Greens Union told Lrytas TV on Sunday that Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius must resign, Elta reported via LRT and Delfi [8] [9]. He said an early election would be acceptable if it came to that [8] [9]. An ethics commission at ISM University of Management and Economics found serious citation and attribution breaches, including plagiarism, in the dissertation [8]. The university ordered Sinkevičius to correct the work within six months [8]. Sinkevičius admitted the citation breaches but said the dissertation still has scientific value [8]. He said the ethics commission considered revoking his degree a disproportionate step [8].
Confidence is moderate: LRT and Delfi both carry the same Elta report of the TV interview; the university's findings and the premier's statement were not read directly.

items.title: Lithuania's Anti-Graft Agency Finds No Sign Civic Group Sought Defense Contract Favors
items.lede: The Nemunas Dawn party had accused the Visuotinė gynyba association of pressuring politicians and the army, and the ethics watchdog will still review lobbying questions.

sections.text: Lithuania's Special Investigation Service (STT) found no data that donors or members of the Visuotinė gynyba association sought special terms in defense procurement, BNS reported via LRT [10]. Nemunas Dawn lawmakers took their complaint to the Prosecutor General's Office, which passed it to the STT [10]. The STT sent the possible lobbying questions to the Chief Official Ethics Commission (VTEK) [10]. VTEK chair Jolanta Bernotaitė said the commission will consider the STT material at its next meeting [10]. She said VTEK declined to open a probe based on a separate referral from the State Security Department, citing a lack of facts [10]. Association head Tomas Godliauskas earlier rejected the claims and said the group aims to boost public resilience [10].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one BNS report carried by LRT quoting agency statements; the STT and VTEK statements were not read directly.

items.title: Estonia's Social Democrats Name Ex-Diplomat Jonatan Vseviov as Their Prime Minister Candidate
items.lede: The former Foreign Ministry chief will lead the party list in Harju and Rapla counties for the 7 March 2027 parliamentary election.

sections.text: The council of Estonia's Social Democratic Party (SDE) endorsed Jonatan Vseviov on Sunday as its candidate for prime minister, ERR and Postimees reported [11] [12]. Vseviov stepped down as secretary general of the Foreign Ministry to run in the election [11]. Party leader Lauri Läänemets proposed the nomination and said support for the party has tripled since the 2023 election [11]. Vseviov called for a more ambitious foreign policy and a stronger Estonian voice in Europe [11]. He said Estonia cannot keep issues off the international agenda by keeping quiet [11]. Läänemets said the party wants to put Estonia back at the heart of Europe [12].
Confidence is high on the nomination: ERR and Postimees both report the council vote; the quotes rest on each outlet's own account.

items.title: Estonia's President Picks Supreme Court Justice Oliver Kask as Chancellor of Justice
items.lede: Kask, a former election committee chair, vowed to keep the ombudsman office nonpolitical as Reform, EKRE, and the Social Democrats set their own tests.

sections.text: Estonian President Ülle Madise proposed to parliament on Saturday that Supreme Court Justice Oliver Kask become the next chancellor of justice, ERR reported [13]. Madise held the post until she took office as president earlier in October [13]. Kask was a Tallinn Circuit Court judge from 2004 to 2024 and joined the Supreme Court in September 2024 [13]. Parliament appoints the chancellor for seven years, and its party groups plan to meet Kask the week after next [14]. Kask told ERR the office must not be political and that political questions belong to parliament and the government [14]. He said he would focus first on social rights for people who struggle to defend themselves in court [14]. The Social Democrats want the chancellor to keep working on personal data protection [14]. EKRE said Kask must prove his independence and defend e-voting oversight [14]. ERR's English service reported Sunday that Kask once chaired Estonia's National Electoral Committee [15]. Reform lawmaker Madis Timpson said the chancellor should push for better laws, not more laws [15]. No vote date was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on three ERR reports quoting the president, the nominee, and party figures; no outlet outside ERR was read.

items.title: Lithuania Stops Taking Work and Study Permit Requests From Many Foreigners Already Inside
items.lede: Visitors on Schengen visas must now file through VFS Global centers abroad, and Belarusians can apply for work permits in Armenia and Georgia.

sections.text: Lithuania's new rules on temporary residence permits for work or bachelor's studies took effect Sunday, LRT reported, citing the Migration Department [16]. Foreigners who entered on a Schengen visa or another country's national visa can no longer file those requests inside Lithuania [16]. Only holders of a Lithuanian permit or national visa, an EU or Schengen residence permit, or visa-free status may still file in the country [16]. Others must apply at centers run by the outside contractor VFS Global [16]. The change does not apply to highly qualified workers [16]. Belarusian citizens can file work-permit requests at VFS Global offices in Armenia and Georgia [16].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one LRT report citing the Migration Department; the department's notice and the amended law were not read directly.

items.title: Iliana Iotova Wins Bulgaria's Presidential Runoff With About 58% of the Vote
items.lede: Rival Andrey Gyurov conceded on Sunday night, she becomes the first woman elected head of state, and official final figures are due within three days.

sections.text: Bulgaria's Central Election Commission (CIK) said Iliana Iotova and running mate Kiril Valchev won 57.661% in Sunday's presidential runoff [1]. Andrey Gyurov and Georgi Kandev won 39.383% [1]. The figures cover 99.68% of tally sheets as of 05:00 Sofia time (04:00 CET) Monday [1]. Iotova had 1,091,206 votes, and Gyurov had 745,303 [1]. Iotova is set to become Bulgaria's first elected woman president, RTÉ reported [2]. With 52.42% counted at midnight Sofia time, BNT reported Iotova at 57.95% [3]. Four polling firms' parallel counts put her between 56.1% and 58.2% [4] [2]. Gyurov said he accepted the results, "however surprising they might be" [5] [2]. Iotova said Gyurov called to congratulate her [6]. She thanked Prime Minister Rumen Radev, who joined her at the briefing [6]. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen congratulated her on X [2]. Turnout was 19.33% at 16:00 Sofia time, and no final turnout figure was published by the cutoff [7]. CIK will announce final results within three days [7]. Police logged 461 reports of suspected violations by midafternoon, mostly about vote-buying [8].
Confidence is high: CIK's own count, BNT, BTA, and RTÉ's wire-based report agree on the winner and margin; the count is preliminary until CIK certifies it.

items.title: Serbia's Repeat Vote Puts Zukorlić's Party in Parliament, Observers Say
items.lede: CRTA says just 12 ballots decided that seat, which costs the Student List one mandate and leaves it with 140.
items.flag: FOLLOW UP TO PREVIOUS REPORT · single-source, unconfirmed

sections.text: Serbia held repeat voting on Sunday at 53 polling stations in 24 cities and municipalities, N1 reported, citing the observer group CRTA [9]. The rerun is part of the 25 October snap parliamentary election [9]. CRTA said its observers recorded isolated cases of pressure on voters [9]. These included vote-buying, parallel voter lists, and third parties at or near polling stations [9]. CRTA said observers in Aleksinac heard claims of vote-buying for the list of Usame Zukorlić's SPP [9]. It said UV lamps were not used properly at some stations in Novi Pazar and Majdanpek [9]. No statement from the Republic Electoral Commission was found by the cutoff. After polls closed at 20:00, CRTA said the rerun changed the seat count from the electoral commission's projection [10]. By its count, Usame Zukorlić's SPP list wins one seat [10]. The Student List drops one seat, to 140, and Aleksandar Vučić's list holds 103 [10]. CRTA said 12 votes decided the SPP seat, which made the vote-buying claims more worrying [10]. Turnout at the 53 stations was 44.9% [10]. Zukorlić said his list won more than 300 votes at the rerun stations [11].
Confidence is moderate: the seat projection is CRTA's own count as relayed by N1, and official commission figures were not found by the cutoff.

items.title: Bulgaria Warns Ships of Drifting Containers Off Burgas After Drone Strike Sinking
items.lede: Four containers were spotted in the Black Sea on Sunday, days after maritime drones sank a cargo ship off Shabla and spilled part of its load.

sections.text: Bulgaria's Vessel Traffic Management and Information System (VTMIS) issued a navigational warning on Sunday about four containers drifting east of Burgas Bay, BTA reported [12]. The containers were sighted at four separate positions at 10:55 [12]. The warning told vessels to proceed with extreme caution [12]. On 28 October, three maritime drones struck a container ship about 21 nautical miles southeast of Shabla [12]. The ship sank around midnight, the Varna Regional Administration said [12]. Navy commander Rear Adm. Kiril Mihaylov said at the time that 20 of the 421 containers aboard had fallen overboard [12]. BTA did not say whether the four containers came from the sunken ship.
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on the VTMIS warning as reported by BTA; no second outlet was checked by the cutoff.

items.title: Armenia's Foreign Minister Pitches Peace and Transit Links to Gulf Forum in Bahrain
items.lede: Ararat Mirzoyan told the Manama Dialogue's closing session that Armenia has chosen peace and that the TRIPP route will link East and West.

sections.text: Armenian Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan met Gulf Cooperation Council Secretary-General Jasem Albudaiwi in Manama, Bahrain, Report.az reported [1]. Mirzoyan posted about the meeting on X on 31 October [1]. He said they discussed closer institutional cooperation and economic ties [1]. They also discussed regional transport links and the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity project [1]. They also discussed how to make peace between Armenia and Azerbaijan more lasting, as well as the situation in the Middle East [1]. On 1 November, Mirzoyan addressed the closing plenary of the Manama Dialogue, Armenia's Foreign Ministry said [2]. Bahrain's foreign minister and UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash also spoke on the panel [2]. Mirzoyan called the August 2025 Washington summit a historic milestone toward peace with Azerbaijan [2]. He said the TRIPP project would bring rail, power, fiber optic, and oil and gas links across Armenia [2].
Confidence is high, as both accounts come from the minister's own post and his ministry's published speech text; no Azerbaijani reaction was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Georgia Says Russian Forces Freed a Citizen Detained Near the South Ossetia Line
items.lede: The State Security Service said the man held near Bershueti in Gori Municipality is back in government-controlled territory after EU monitors' hotline was used.

sections.text: Georgia's State Security Service (SSG) said on Sunday that a Georgian citizen detained by Russian forces near the village of Bershueti has been released, Interpressnews reported [3]. Bershueti is in Gori Municipality, near the line with Russian-occupied South Ossetia [3]. The SSG statement dated the case to 31 October and said the man is now in territory controlled by the central government [3]. The SSG said it used all available mechanisms, including the hotline run by the EU Monitoring Mission in Georgia (EUMM) [3]. It said it is working to free all Georgian citizens held in the occupied territories [3]. The statement did not name the man or say how long he was held.
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on the SSG statement as relayed by Interpressnews; no EUMM or Tskhinvali comment was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Needles Turn Up in Halloween Candy in Five German States
items.lede: Police have no suspects yet and are telling parents to keep any tampered sweets and wrappers so investigators can check them for traces.

sections.text: Police in five German states are investigating Halloween candy spiked with needles and other metal parts, Deutschlandfunk reported [1]. In Baden-Württemberg, two families in Filderstadt found needles in hazelnut bars on Saturday [2]. Police said the needles appeared to be placed on purpose and could not be seen from outside [2]. Metal objects were also found in wrapped wafer bars in Rielasingen-Worblingen, near Konstanz [2]. Police urged parents to check their children's candy and keep any suspect items with the packaging [2].

Confidence is moderate: the Baden-Württemberg cases rest on police statements reported by Stuttgarter Zeitung, while the five-state count comes from a short Deutschlandfunk item. No suspects or injuries were reported by the cutoff.

items.title: German Cyber Agency Warns Lawmakers and Ministers of Spyware on Their iPhones
items.lede: Digital Minister Karsten Wildberger confirmed the alert, which stems from Apple threat notices received since 29 October, but no one knows yet who is behind it.

sections.text: Germany's federal cyber agency, the BSI, warned members of parliament and of the government about a possible spyware attack on their phones [3] [4] [5]. ARD first reported the warning on Sunday [3]. Digital Minister Karsten Wildberger confirmed it on ARD's Sunday evening politics show [3]. He said Apple had flagged that certain devices may have been compromised [3]. The agency's letter says affected iPhones have received Apple threat notices since 29 October [3]. The notices warn of so-called mercenary spyware [3]. The BSI said it has no details on the cause [3]. It told recipients to assume their devices may be compromised [3]. The names of those affected have not been made public [3]. Apple does not say what triggers its notices or name attackers [3].

Confidence is high on the warning, which the digital minister confirmed on air and which tagesschau, Stuttgarter Zeitung via dpa, and Deutschlandfunk reported. No attacker has been named, and it is not known whether any attack succeeded.

items.title: IG Metall Widens Warning Strikes to Seven German States on Monday
items.lede: Bavaria alone has 34 plants on the strike list, and employers say the walkouts do needless damage while the union seeks a 5% raise.

sections.text: Germany's IG Metall union began warning strikes in the metal and electrical industry just after midnight, when a no-strike obligation expired [6] [7]. About 300 night-shift workers at thyssenkrupp Rasselstein in Andernach, Rhineland-Palatinate, stopped work and rallied at the plant gate [6] [7]. A walkout also began at RF360 Europe/Qualcomm, a mobile-phone parts supplier in Munich [7]. Regional union leader Joerg Koehlinger called the Andernach walkout the start of a massive strike phase [6]. The union had said a large Bavarian carmaker will be hit for the first time on Monday [8]. IG Metall wants a 5% raise over 12 months and job guarantees for about 3.7 million workers [7] [9]. Employers have offered a one-time payment next year and a 1.3% raise in 2028 [9] [6]. Night-shift workers also walked out at auto supplier KSM Castings in Hildesheim, Lower Saxony [10]. Union leader Christiane Benner has promised strong warning strikes [10]. The union called walkouts for Monday at plants in Berlin, Hamburg, Lower Saxony, North Rhine-Westphalia, Brandenburg, Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, and Bavaria [11] [12]. Bavaria alone has 34 plants on the list, including auto factories [11]. Employer group Gesamtmetall called the strikes needless damage [11].
Confidence is high on the strike calls, reported by tagesschau and Deutschlandfunk from union statements. Monday turnout figures were not available by the cutoff.

items.title: Frankfurt Police Report 54 Arrests and 100 Officers Hurt After Germany's Gen Z Rallies
items.lede: A cabinet split has opened over who caused the looting, with Defense Minister Boris Pistorius rejecting the interior minister's blame on migrant groups.

sections.text: Germany's 'Gen Z regelt' youth rallies in more than 30 cities stayed mostly peaceful on Saturday [13] [14]. Frankfurt police said Sunday they had made 54 arrests and recorded 87 criminal complaints [15]. About 100 officers were hurt, and five stores were looted [15] [16]. Police blamed the later looting mainly on known groups of young men who meet downtown on weekends, many with immigrant backgrounds [15]. Hesse Interior Minister Roman Poseck said those arrested are 13 to 29 years old and mostly German citizens [15]. In Baden-Württemberg, the state interior ministry reported nine officers hurt and seven people detained among almost 15,000 marchers [17]. Federal Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt blamed "violent left-wing groups" and "troublemakers from the migrant milieu" and called for tough sentences [18]. The organizers distanced themselves from the violence and plan new protests on 20 November [19] [14]. Defense Minister Boris Pistorius, a Social Democrat, questioned Dobrindt's wording on ZDF Sunday evening [20] [21]. "What are migrant groups?" he asked, noting that many are third-generation German citizens [20]. He said extremists who attack police must be punished [20].
Confidence is high on the Frankfurt figures, which come from a police and ministry press conference reported by tagesschau and Deutschlandfunk. The Pistorius quotes come from tagesschau, citing ZDF.

items.title: Germany's New Military Combat Helicopters Will Fly Without Weapons for Now, Spiegel Says
items.lede: The report is a setback for Defense Minister Boris Pistorius, who is buying ready-made equipment to rebuild the Bundeswehr quickly.

sections.text: Germany's new military combat helicopters can fly but will not be able to fire weapons for the foreseeable future, Der Spiegel reported Sunday [22]. The magazine cited its own information [22]. Defense Minister Boris Pistorius wants to rearm the Bundeswehr at record speed [22]. His plan relies on weapons already on the market rather than new designs [22]. Spiegel said the helicopter purchase was one of the first showcase projects of that approach [22]. It said the plan did not work in this case [22].
Confidence is low because only Spiegel has reported this, and only the article's summary was available behind its paywall. The defense ministry had not commented in the material seen by the cutoff.

items.title: Germany Misses Its Legal Gas Storage Target With Sites About 61% Full
items.lede: The government and the network regulator say winter supply is safe thanks to new import terminals, while a Greens lawmaker says there is no safety buffer.

sections.text: Germany's gas storage sites were about 61.2% full on Sunday, short of the 70% average the law requires by 1 November, according to European AGSI data [23]. The economy ministry said winter supply remains secure [23]. Federal Network Agency head Klaus Müller said meeting the storage targets is no longer essential for secure supply [23] [24]. He pointed to Germany's liquefied natural gas terminals [23]. The agency said it sees no need to act [23]. Greens energy lawmaker Michael Kellner accused Economy Minister Katherina Reiche of poor planning [23]. He said storage levels are the lowest ever and leave no safety buffer [23]. An industry association warned of possible shortages [24]. Timm Kehler of the gas and hydrogen industry association said missing the target carries no penalty [23][25].

Confidence is high on the fill level and official statements, reported by tagesschau and Deutschlandfunk. The fill figure comes from AGSI data as cited by tagesschau and was not checked against the platform directly.

items.title: German Prosecutor Andrés Ritter Takes Charge of the EU's Fraud Prosecution Office
items.lede: The former deputy chief now leads the Luxembourg agency that pursues customs and tax fraud against the bloc's budget.

sections.text: German prosecutor Andrés Ritter became European Chief Prosecutor on Sunday [26]. His seven-year term at the European Public Prosecutor's Office in Luxembourg began on 1 November [26]. EU governments and the European Parliament approved his nomination in the spring [26]. Ritter was deputy to Romania's Laura Kövesi, who led the office for seven years [26]. He previously ran the economic and cybercrime prosecutor's office in Rostock, in the northeastern German state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania [26]. The office investigates fraud against the EU budget [26]. Its investigators had a record 3,602 active cases at the end of 2025, with estimated damage of about 67 billion euros [26]. Most of the damage comes from customs and value-added tax fraud [26]. Twenty-five EU countries take part [26].

Confidence is high on the appointment, which DW reported with dpa photos and which follows a confirmation process completed in the spring. The case figures come from the office's annual report as cited by DW.
